entities.name: Query spastin-like ATPase
observations: 661 aa, basic protein with predicted molecular mass ~72.7 kDa and pI ~9.59.
Contains one prominent hydrophobic segment near residues ~90–145, consistent with an intramembrane hairpin or membrane anchor rather than a multipass membrane protein.
Contains a strong AAA ATPase domain at residues 421–550, an AAA lid region at 577–611, and a Vps4_C region at 621–657.
Matches reviewed Drosophila spastin proteins at ~58% identity over ~93% query coverage; this supports a spastin-family assignment.
Likely forms an oligomeric ring and severs microtubules using ATP hydrolysis; exact organism-specific biology is inferred from homologs, not directly demonstrated for this sequence.

entities.name: Spastin microtubule severing
observations: ATP-dependent reaction represented as n ATP + n H2O + microtubule -> n ADP + n phosphate + (n+1) alpha/beta tubulin heterodimers.
This is a mechanical AAA+ ATPase reaction coupled to microtubule lattice disassembly, rather than conventional covalent substrate turnover.

entities.name: Drosophila spastin homologs
observations: Reviewed homologs B4HGG6, Q8I0P1, and B3P8A3 are annotated as ATP-dependent microtubule-severing proteins with EC 5.6.1.1, ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis, microtubule binding, and microtubule-severing ATPase activity.
Homologs are reported as hexameric AAA+ proteins with membrane association and cytoskeletal localization.
